summary: Nicol Macnicol (1870–1952) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He was educated at the High School of Glasgow and the University of Glasgow (M.A. c. 1887–1891, D.Litt. 1901), and served as a missionary at Wilson College, Mumbai, from 1895.
Nicola Bajetta is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, he conducted doctoral research and served as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter at the University of Hamburg.

Nicola Di Cosmo (born 1957) is a sinology, Iranian and Central Asian, and history and archaeology scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Indiana University Bloomington (c. 1985–1991). He held appointments at Harvard, Columbia, and the Institute for Advanced Study.

Nicolaas Johannes Krom (1883–1945) specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (Ph.D. 1908) under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Jacob Samuel Speyer, later serving in the Netherlands East Indies Archaeological Service and as a Leiden professor.

Nicolaas van Wijk (1880–1942) was a linguist who studied under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck, Karl Brugmann, August Leskien, and Filipp Fortunatov at Amsterdam, Leipzig, and Moscow. He worked at the National Library of the Netherlands before becoming a Leiden University professor in 1913.
Nicolas Morrissey is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Gregory Schopen. He holds a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Silpakorn University and under supervisors including Claudine Bautze-Picron, Peter Skilling, and Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h, and held a post at Thammasat University.
Nicolas Sihlé is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant professor in the Department of Anthropology at the University of Virginia.

Nicolas Tournadre (born 1959) is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned his Ph.D. under Claude Hagège at Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He held positions at INALCO, Paris 8, the University of Provence, and Aix-Marseille University.
Nicole Baden (born 1981) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under Richard Baker as a traditional teacher and succeeded him in 2024.
Nicole Balbir (1924–2008) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Charlotte Vaudeville. She held academic posts at Patna University from 1952 to 1955 and at INALCO from 1974 to 1992.

Nicole Karapanagiotis is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She has held posts at Rutgers University–Camden and serves as an Associate Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Rutgers University.

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas (1906–1987) was a sinologist and scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She taught Chinese art at the École du Louvre (c. 1944–1976) and was a professor of Chinese civilization at INALCO.

Nicolás Altuchow (1912–1983) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Stefan Bolesław Stasiak. He taught linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of the Republic from 1951 to 1982 and held a post at the National Museum of Natural History.
Nidheesh Kannan B. is an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (2016–2018), where he became an Assistant Professor in 2021.

Niels Ludvig Westergaard (1815–1878) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Copenhagen, Bonn under Christian Lassen, Paris, and Oxford, he served as professor of Indian-Oriental philology and rector at the University of Copenhagen.

Niels Studsgaard Fuglsang (1759–1832) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Copenhagen in 1778. He served as a minister at Zion Church in Tranquebar (1792–1804) and became a member of The Asiatic Society in 1801.
Nigel Allan is a history and archaeology specialist. He succeeded Marianne Winder and served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust, attested in 1993.

Niharranjan Ray (1903–1981) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Calcutta, UCL, and Leiden under Jean Philippe Vogel, he served as Bageswari Professor at Calcutta University and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

Nijun Zhang is a religious studies and Tibetology scholar. After earning a B.A. at Beijing Foreign Studies University and an M.A. at the University of Pittsburgh, Zhang became a Ph.D. student at the University of Virginia.
